N01: I’m filing a chargeback.” Every small online seller knows this message.
N02: The proof is in four places: the payment provider, the orders database, the server logs, the mail provider.
At one in the morning, that’s four dashboards.
N03: Paste the message. Just the customer’s email — no order number.
N04: Nemotron, through Meterless Nightshift, decides where to look. No order under this email. So: who paid at the payment provider?
Which order is that payment? Then the full journey. Every lookup is read-only, through one SQL door — Zetaris.
N05: A rule-based verifier — not the model — checks the money chain. Paid. Order confirmed. But the credits went to a typo — exmaple dot com — and the mail bounced.
Every red link carries the rows that prove it, and the one query that fetched them.
N05b: And the model’s explanation is checked sentence by sentence: every
amount and address it states must appear in the rows it cites.
N06: You get a reply in the customer’s language. It can’t promise refunds — money is a human decision.
And a fix: move the credits, once the customer confirms.
N07: Approve, and the fix runs. The chain turns green, and the fix goes into an audit log.
N08: And when nothing is broken, it says so: you were never charged.
N08b: And if a message quotes someone else’s order number, that order is never read.
N09: Under the hood: the shop database, the payment provider’s ledger and the mail provider’s events are three separate sources in Zetaris, joined in one semantic layer and read with a single query.
Every model call goes through Nightshift, with a receipt for which model ran. Addresses are masked and card digits removed before any row reaches the model.
N10: Six cases, rebuilt from real bugs in our own shop with synthetic
data: six out of six right, every explanation cited.
N11: Paid, but nothing arrived? Found in one pass.
